title: Iranian coup d'etat of 1953
summary: A covert operation planned by the CIA with British intelligence, known as Operation Ajax, removed Iranian Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddeq in August 1953. A first attempt on 15 August failed, but on 19 August his premiership ended and General Zahedi replaced him; the shah returned on 23 August. The CIA publicly acknowledged its role in 2013. Mosaddeq was convicted of treason.

where.historical_name: Tehran, capital of Iran under Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi

importance.justification: A US-British covert operation that ended Mosaddeq's government and restored the shah, with lasting effects on Iran and on later US interventions.
